channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Oil Futures Pick Up as Middle East Tensions Persist
item.description: Oil prices settled higher for a second straight session with continuing tensions in the Middle East countering expectations of a coming global supply surplus.

item.title: Inside the Scramble to Avert Conflict With Russia in the Baltic
item.description: Two Nordic leaders, with the help of an oligarch, sought out a direct line to Vladimir Putin to ease fears about a NATO blockade of the crucial waterway.

item.title: Army Detonates Tons of Toxic Lead Explosives in Iowa
item.description: Residents within 20 miles who haven’t evacuated should shelter in place, federal officials said.

item.title: Fragrance Giants Handed $630 Million in EU, U.K. Antitrust Fines
item.description: The EU said that the world’s three largest fragrance groups exchanged commercially sensitive information, including on pricing and their dealings with consumer giant Unilever.

item.title: BOE’s Bailey Sees Lower Peak for Inflation if Energy Prices Stay Where They Are
item.description: The U.K.’s annual rate of inflation would peak at a lower level than the Bank of England had forecast if prices of oil and natural gas were to stay where they are, Governor Andrew Bailey said.

item.title: EU Lays out Plan to Boost Quantum Technology
item.description: Officials are also targeting the establishment of a $55 billion Sovereign Tech Equity Fund as part of a broader push to strengthen Europe’s tech independence.

item.title: China Takes Down Shanghai Party Boss Once Seen as Potential Leader
item.description: Chen Jining, the party secretary of Shanghai, has been placed under investigation on suspicion of severe violations of party discipline and state laws.

item.title: China’s Military Ambitions in the Pacific Suffer Setback
item.description: The Solomon Islands said it won’t allow foreign bases on its soil, calming worries that the country was slipping into China’s orbit and that Beijing could open a military outpost there.

item.title: Shapiro Accuses Biden of Not Doing Enough to Rein In Netanyahu
item.description: The Pennsylvania governor said Biden didn’t go far enough to constrain Netanyahu in his first interview on foreign policy ahead of a potential 2028 run.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis Take Second Swipe at Tallest Tower in Saudi Capital
item.description: The strike on the Public Investment Fund Tower follows a previous Houthi assault on the building on Thursday.

item.title: China’s Huawei Convicted of Fraud in U.S. Criminal Trial
item.description: A federal jury convicted the tech and telecom giant of fraud and other offenses but acquitted it of racketeering conspiracy.

item.title: Venezuela Reveals an Eye-Popping Debt Load of $237 Billion
item.description: The higher-than-expected figure underscores the challenges faced by the U.S.-backed interim government.

item.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Shipping Risks Persist
item.description: Oil prices picked up from initial losses and settled higher Tuesday as traders weighed persistent threats to energy shipments in the Middle East against expectations of a global supply surplus.

item.title: Huang Tells Staff He Is in Therapy, Apologizes in Nvidia Town Hall
item.description: The Nvidia co-founder thanked the Trump administration while addressing staff the day after he was reinstated as CEO.

item.title: I Went Inside Chornobyl as Ukraine Races to Secure It
item.description: Watch how Ukrainian engineers and the armed forces are racing to contain radiation at the nuclear power plant.

item.title: British Police Arrest Two Men Over Suspected Burglary at Royal Estate
item.description: The police searched the estate where Prince William and Kate have a country home.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: U.S. Chip Restrictions Amplify Shell Company Headaches in AI Ecosystem
item.description: Plus: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and new study raises Bayer cancer link again

item.title: Russian Warplanes Trigger Alarm Among U.S. Partners in Asia
item.description: Military aircraft has skirted or entered the airspace of U.S. allies in Asia several times in recent days, prompting Japan and South Korea to scramble jet fighters.

item.title: The Gap Between China’s Military Spectacle and Battlefield Reality
item.description: Plus, U.S. chip restrictions deepen China’s AI computing crunch and the shadow network behind Nvidia’s China chip-smuggling scandal resurfaces.
